content.text:
I submitted **index 61** (Cr 0.079, Fe 0.406, V 0.515), which gave the highest EQE I measured: **0.209%**. I don't know how close that is to the best composition in the library.

I spent all 3 merit measurements. My choice of where to look came from memory, not from the library: I picked the region where Fe and V are roughly equal, since that's the FeVO₄ photoanode phase, and I recall published work adding a little Cr to it. With Fe held at about 0.41, EQE rose each time Cr went down:

| Index | Cr | Fe | V | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 103 | 0.153 | 0.412 | 0.435 | 0.141 |
| 75 | 0.099 | 0.411 | 0.491 | 0.194 |
| 61 | 0.079 | 0.406 | 0.515 | 0.209 |

- **The trend hadn't levelled off when the budget ran out.** EQE was still rising as Cr fell, so a nearby composition with even less Cr (e.g. index 47 or 62) might score higher.
- **Most of the library went untested.** All three measurements were in one small region. I ruled out the Cr-rich and V-rich regions by reasoning only.
- **I didn't use the XRD budget (0 of 5).** So I have no evidence that the FeVO₄ phase is actually present in these films.
